title: Chat stream demultiplexer and developer signals for Python SDK
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: the current Python SDK streaming chat surface exposes a flat stream of raw events (text delta chunks, function_call fragments, partial metadata). Integrators repeatedly implement the same plumbing to: 1) group partial deltas into coherent messages, 2) separate control signals (function_call, tool-invoke, finish_reason) from text, 3) surface retryable checkpoints and backpressure hooks, and 4) expose a concise consumer contract that works sync and async. This ticket proposes a small, backwards-compatible utility layer (ChatStreamDemux) and a set of lightweight developer signal helpers to standardize those patterns.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New ChatStreamDemux provides a typed iterator/async-iterator that yields high-level events: TextDelta, MessageComplete, FunctionCallStart/Append/End, Checkpoint(token), Error and RetryHint. 2) Demux preserves existing raw event access via `.raw()` on events for debugging. 3) Sync and async APIs have identical semantics and ergonomics. 4) Built-in helpers for merging partial chunks and assembling function_call payloads with tests. 5) Small example in docs demonstrating: resumable stream checkpoint, applying idempotent retry, and wiring a UI consumer callback without manual delta-assembling. 6) No breaking changes to existing public SDK method signatures.
design_notes:
- Keep the top-level Stream API unchanged: users who already consume the raw event stream continue to work. ChatStreamDemux is an opt-in adapter.
- Provide both iterator-based consumption and a callback mode (on_event) to support UI apps that want push semantics.
- Use lightweight Python dataclasses for events, but do not introduce heavy dependency; keep serialization simple. Events will expose `type` and `as_text()`/`as_json()` helpers.
- Checkpointing API: emit Checkpoint(token) every N tokens or on message boundaries. Token is an opaque string produced by server; client stores it for retries/resume.
- Retry semantics: demux will emit RetryHint(reason, idempotency_key) when it detects retriable network errors; higher-level retry util will accept checkpoint and resume.
- Backpressure: demux exposes a configurable max_buffer_tokens and an async-friendly `pause()`/`resume()` contract used by SDK runtime to honor consumer slowness.
- Tradeoffs: adding adapter increases surface area and docs burden but greatly reduces per-app duplication. Avoid heavy typing to keep API stable across minor runtime changes.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype ChatStreamDemux module implementing sync iterator that wraps existing raw_event_generator (2 days). 2) Add async iterator parity + pause/resume hooks (2 days). 3) Unit tests for chunk assembly, function_call assembly, and checkpointing logic (2 days). 4) End-to-end integration test using recorded streaming fixture and a small resume scenario (1 day). 5) Docs + example notebook demonstrating resume & retry patterns (1 day). 6) Open PR, address feedback, and ship behind feature flag in py-sdk-2.6 (2 days).
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: subtle ordering bugs when merging partial deltas across interleaved function_call and text events. Mitigation: build extensive unit fixtures from real server traces and add property tests.
- Risk: consumers relying on low-level timing of raw events could observe behavior differences. Mitigation: preserve `.raw()` on demuxed events and document differences; default to opt-in.
- Risk: checkpoint token format changes from server. Mitigation: treat token as opaque string and include a small compatibility shim when server version mismatches are detected.
